newsArray.title: Congress' 'Communal Spin' After Siraj Dropped Sparks Debate
newsArray.description: The exclusion of fast bowler Mohammed Siraj from India's playing XI for the first Test against New Zealand has sparked a political controversy. The decision, which some cricket experts have questioned on performance grounds, has been given a communal angle by opposition leaders, including Congress MP Imran Masood. Masood alleged that Siraj was dropped due to his religion, a claim that has drawn sharp criticism from the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and other commentators. Congress' 'Communal Spin' After Siraj Dropped Imran Masood, a Congress leader and close ally of Rahul Gandhi, suggested that Siraj's exclusion was influenced by his Muslim identity. This statement was echoed by other opposition figures, including members of the All India Majlis-e-Ittehad-ul-Muslimeen (AIMIM) and the Samajwadi Party, who expanded the allegations to include broader claims of discrimination. However, the BJP has dismissed these accusations, arguing that team selection is based solely on merit and performance. The party also pointed out that other players, such as Ravindra Jadeja, who is affiliated with the BJP, were also left out of the squad. Political Reactions and Broader Implications The BJP has accused the Congress of using cricket as a tool for vote-bank politics, particularly with elections in Uttar Pradesh on the horizon. BJP spokespersons have argued that the opposition is attempting to create a communal narrative around cricket to appeal to specific voter bases. Meanwhile, cricketing legends have expressed their surprise at Siraj's exclusion but have refrained from attributing it to religious discrimination. The controversy has reignited debates about the intersection of sports and politics in India, with critics urging political parties to avoid communalizing issues related to national representation.

newsArray.title: Yuzvendra Chahal Joins BJP, Gets Role In Party's OBC Morcha National Executive
newsArray.description: Indian cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal has joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and been appointed a special invitee to the national executive of the party’s Other Backwards Classes (OBC) Morcha, the BJP announced on Saturday. Expressing gratitude over his appointment, Chahal thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP national president Nitin Nabin and OBC Morcha national president Amar Pal Maurya for welcoming him into the party. In a post on X in Hindi, the leg-spinner said he was deeply grateful to the party leadership for giving him a place in the BJP family and honouring him with the responsibility. Chahal had earlier met Maurya, a Rajya Sabha MP. He is expected to represent Delhi in his new role. The BJP has also appointed Professor Advait Charan Gananayak from Odisha and advocate Seema Samriddhi Kushwaha from Uttar Pradesh as special invitees to the OBC Morcha's national executive. BJP Announces New OBC Morcha Office-Bearers Along with the special invitees, the BJP named 37 members to the OBC Morcha's national executive. The party also appointed seven national vice-presidents, three national general secretaries and seven national secretaries. The appointments, approved by BJP national president Nitin Nabin, came into effect immediately, according to the party. Among the new national vice-presidents is Jogen Mohan from Assam. The other appointees are Mamata Mohanta from Odisha, Sangam Lal Gupta and Sangeeta Balwant Bind from Uttar Pradesh, Babanrao Raoji Chaudhary from Maharashtra, Sat Prakash Rana from Delhi and Arjun Sahni from Bihar. Gajendra Yadav from Delhi, Pramod Madhwaraj from Karnataka and Lalit Chandrakar from Chhattisgarh have been appointed national general secretaries. The party named Dashrathji Thakor from Gujarat, T Varatharajan from Tamil Nadu, Sanjeev Kumar from Jharkhand, Sarita Jangid from Haryana, Kadaganchi Ramesh from Telangana, Vaibhav Panwar from Madhya Pradesh and Bhim Kumar Sahu from Bihar as national secretaries. The organisational appointments come ahead of Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Manipur and Goa. Yuzvendra Chahal's Cricket Career Chahal made his international debut for India in 2016 and has established himself as one of the country's leading limited-overs leg-spinners. He has taken 121 wickets in 72 One-Day Internationals (ODIs) and 96 wickets in 80 T20 Internationals. One of the notable performances of his international career came in 2017, when he claimed six wickets for 25 runs against England in Bengaluru. He became the first Indian bowler to take five or more wickets in a men's T20 International. Chahal also picked up 12 wickets in eight matches during the 2019 ODI World Cup and was part of India's squad that won the T20 World Cup in 2024. In the Indian Premier League (IPL), he has represented Mumbai Indians, Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Rajasthan Royals and Punjab Kings. He surpassed Dwayne Bravo to become the IPL's leading wicket-taker in 2023. A year later, while playing for Rajasthan Royals, he became the first bowler to reach the 200-wicket mark in the tournament. In October 2026, Chahal announced his retirement from first-class cricket after taking 148 wickets in 49 matches. However, he said he remained hopeful of representing India again in ODIs and T20 Internationals.
